patch.title: Aldrin 138 BESS: 207 MW Queue Scope, March 2028 Target
patch.description: ERCOT lists Aldrin 138 BESS request 25INR0421, Aldrin Energy Storage LLC, 207 MW in Brazoria County, targeting March 1, 2028 with studies complete and IA reported. Vesper’s current Aldrin site describes a broader 550 MW / 1,100 MWh proposal in active development, as soon as early 2028.

references.title: ERCOT September 2026 GIS — Aldrin 138 BESS 25INR0421
Vesper Energy — Aldrin Energy Storage current project scope
Aldrin Energy Storage — FAQ

patch.longFormSummary:
• The request POI is North Alvin TNMP 138 kV, bus 39015. The two requests’ 207 MW and 362 MW are not silently equated to the operator’s broader 550 MW scope, and its 1,100 MWh is not divided between requests. No four-hour or per-request battery MWh verified. The current operator says site planning/review, not completed construction.
  • The former $210M / $360M costs are unsupported. Aldrin 345 was incorrectly assigned 25INR0422, which is Waterloo Solar 1 in Bastrop; its correct ID is 25INR0425, and the prior June 2028 target is replaced by March 2028. Regional road photos and the operator’s Energia Basica-branded battery illustration are not verified Aldrin request-specific facility photos.
  • Timeline: March 1, 2028 is ERCOT projected COD. Operator says as soon as early 2028 without an exact day; neither proves actual energization.

patch.title: Allthorn Battery: 200 MW / 400 MWh in 2029 Hybrid Plan
patch.description: Palladium’s September 2026 sale teaser publishes Allthorn at 230 MWac solar and 200 MW / 400 MWh two-hour storage, targeting Q3 2029. Its adviser says draft SGIAs await execution; ERCOT separately reports 231.5 MW solar and 205.2 MW battery, targeting January 15, 2029.

references.title: Palladium / Fractal — Projects Indigo and Allthorn, September 2026 teaser
Palladium Portfolio Sale – ERCOT South PV+S
ERCOT September 2026 GIS — Allthorn 28INR0230

patch.longFormSummary:
• The teaser explicitly labels development-stage projects and publishes 436.7 MW POI available capacity, 2,500-acre maximum lease option, AEP 138 kV line and location 27°23′44.4″N 98°41′47.5″W. These are proposed commercial scopes, not surveyed as-built boundaries, installed export or a guaranteed rating. Native power uses only this pin’s component.
  • The adviser’s 2025 construction-commencement claim is accompanied by transformer purchase and December 2025 beginning-of-construction inspection for tax eligibility; it is not proof of full physical build or operation. ERCOT still says full study started/no IA, consistent with draft SGIA pending. The former four-hour / 821 MWh battery and $200M / $240M budgets are unsupported.
  • Timeline: Confirmed September 16, 2026 sale-process announcement, not COD. Teaser Q3 2029 and queue January 15, 2029 are differing projected schedules; no exact future service day adopted.
  • September 2026 preliminary Allthorn hybrid project overview, PDF page 3: proposed capacity, project location, lease-option acreage and target COD. The same hybrid diagram supplies context to solar and battery components; not an as-built boundary or photograph. Credit: Palladium Energy / Fractal Business Analytics; underlying map credits as shown.

patch.description: Aligned lists PHX-07 at 8785 N Reems Road, Waddell, separate from its Union Hills campus. Contractor Lewis describes PHX 07-2 as the second phase of an 80 MW project; that phase adds 40 MW IT across six halls within a 214,078-sqft building.

Aligned breaks ground on data center in Phoenix, Arizona

• Native 80 MW is the contractor’s two-phase project scope, not the entire West Valley campus, measured facility demand or an additional 80 MW above phase two. The 214,078 sqft is PHX 07-2 only and is not assigned as whole PHX07 area. No installed generator count or daily water use inferred from standard module ratings.
  • The April 17, 2025 report describes a prospective later-2025 PHX07 opening; that is not realized COD. It separately discusses PHX13 and the broader 100-acre land purchase; neither its area nor $86.5M land price is a PHX07-only building budget. Removed $3.04B, modeled 92 MW, December 2027 COD and unsupported Union Hills utility claims.
  • Timeline: Confirmed April 17, 2025 dated report describing PHX07’s then-prospective later-2025 opening. Saved publication milestone, not exact COD; actual commissioning remains unverified.

patch.title: Aligned LBB-01: First Caprock Building, Q1 2027 Target
patch.description: Aligned’s April 9, 2026 groundbreaking announcement explicitly names LBB-01 as the first facility on its proposed 540 MW, 313-acre, six-facility Caprock campus, targeting Q1 2027 service. Its current LBB-01 address is 1498 County Road 315, Abernathy, rather than Plainview.

references.title: Aligned Data Centers Breaks Ground on “Project Caprock,” a Sustainable 540 MW Next-Generation Data Center Campus in Northwest Texas
Aligned Abernathy: Built for Scale in Northwest Texas

patch.longFormSummary:
• The 540 MW, 1.65 million sqft, 313 acres and expected $5B regional economic infusion are campus/program scope. None establishes a 108 MW / 96 MW IT LBB01 rating, building-only area or $3.42B construction cost. Do not divide campus capacity by six to invent a building rating; native power removed.
  • Operator specifies air-cooled heat rejection and closed-loop DeltaFlow liquid cooling with dedicated power infrastructure; no current absolute daily water reading or named Xcel/SPP service basis is assigned to this building. The release announces the groundbreaking, not completion or a December 2028 COD.
  • Timeline: Confirmed April 9, 2026 campus-groundbreaking announcement explicitly naming first facility LBB01; Q1 2027 remains a target, not actual COD.
  • Operator-published Project Caprock campus groundbreaking photograph. Whole-campus ceremony context; not a photograph of an energized LBB01 or a building-only budget. Credit: Aligned Data Centers.

patch.title: Allium Solar: 110 MW Operator Plan, Conflicting 2029–2030 Targets
patch.description: Longroad’s Allium page proposes 110 MW solar plus a separate 110 MW battery on approximately 945 acres north of Hollister airport. Its timeline targets operation near the end of 2029; active CAISO request 1921 instead targets December 15, 2030, with 110 MW combined export.

references.title: Allium Solar and Energy Storage System Project — Longroad Energy
CAISO Public Queue — active Allium Hybrid 1921 / withdrawn Allium 1711

patch.longFormSummary:
• CAISO reports 112.491 MW solar and 112.386 MW battery separately, export 110 MW, at Crazy Horse Canyon–Hollister 115 kV. Native 110 MW uses operator solar scope only. The prior ID 1532 and Panoche 230 kV attribution are incorrect; withdrawn Allium 1711 is a previous request, not cancellation of active 1921.
  • The operator timeline image targets fall-2025 application, studies into 2027, Q2-2027 approval, end-2027 construction and near-end-2029 operation; these are targets, not completed milestones. No $150M or December 2027 COD. The map places the proposal between Bolsa/SR25 and San Felipe roads north of the airport; the old point near Panoche was far away. Operator four-hour capability statement is not an explicit installed 440 MWh rating.
  • Timeline: December 15, 2030 is active CAISO projected completion; current operator timeline instead shows near-end-2029 operation. Both remain prospective and the conflict is explicit.
  • Longroad proposed Allium site overlay on aerial imagery north of Hollister airport, between Bolsa and San Felipe roads; not a surveyed approved boundary or constructed solar plant. Credit: Longroad Energy; underlying map credits as shown.
  • Longroad Allium projected timeline: end-2027 construction and near-end-2029 operations. These are prospective dates and conflict with the active CAISO December-2030 target. Credit: Longroad Energy; underlying map credits as shown.
  • Longroad Allium community outreach booth at Hollister Farmer’s Market, as identified by the operator; community-engagement context, not a facility photograph. Credit: Longroad Energy; underlying map credits as shown.

researchNotes: Ten existing pins corrected and two individual-building tracker splits soft-deleted/held on local and production. Initial title/source/author identities matched across environments; reconciled stale local IDs, re-read immediately before each write, retained backups and preserved original authors. No new pins or automatic merges. Draft/held catalogs and posted maps synchronized after both environments verified.

Read primary August 2026 EIA inventory, September 2026 ERCOT GIS workbook and CAISO workbook rows. Wrong IDs are replaced by exact name-matched requests, not treated as evidence of cancellation. Queue studies, executed agreements, commercial proposals, tax commencement, actual construction and operating status are separate findings.

Buzzer Butte 2: ERCOT 30INR0164 supports 242.8 MW, Origis Development LLC, Kent County, September 1, 2030 target, screening/full study started without IA, Nova Prime–Mhos 345 kV tap. Removed $250M and unsupported construction implications. No exact-name EIA plant match, parcel filing or verified official facility photo found. County/project-area point retained with qualification.

Aldrin 138: request 25INR0421, 207 MW, North Alvin TNMP 138 kV bus 39015, Brazoria County, studies complete/IA and March 1, 2028 target. Aldrin 345 is 25INR0425, 362 MW at Meadow 345 kV bus 43030, with same target; the original 25INR0422 belongs to Waterloo Solar 1, Bastrop. Two real queue requests remain separate. Vesper’s newly refreshed Aldrin site describes the broader 550 MW / 1,100 MWh, approximately 16-acre proposal, site planning/local-state review and as soon as early-2028 operation. The earlier 2025 construction wording is stale; the old business-partnership URL now returns 404. Do not silently equate 569 MW total requests with the 550 MW operator proposal, divide 1,100 MWh between requests, or retain invented four-hour 828 / 1,448 MWh. Cleared $210M / $360M; June 2028 Aldrin 345 target corrected to March.

Allthorn: downloaded September 2026 Palladium/Fractal sale teaser and opened September 16 adviser announcement. Proposed 230 MWac PV / 200 MW battery / 400 MWh usable at POI / two-hour duration, 436.7 MW POI available capacity, Q3 2029 target, draft SGIA pending execution, 2,500-acre maximum lease option, AEP 138 kV. ERCOT separately lists 231.5 MW solar / 205.2 MW battery, January 15, 2029, full study started/no IA. Both ratings/schedules remain explicit; native components use published commercial proposal 230 and 200 MW. The adviser’s 2025 construction-commencement wording is accompanied by transformer purchase and beginning-of-construction inspection for tax eligibility; it is not proof of full physical build-out. Removed four-hour 821 MWh and $200M / $240M. No completed sale or new owner inferred from an expired bid deadline.

Allthorn published project point 27°23′44.4″N / 98°41′47.5″W replaces both far-north county guesses. It is shared hybrid location, not surveyed battery/solar component boundaries. One preliminary project-overview page is rendered from full PDF page 3 and credited on both component pins using separate Azure files; these are two placements of the same diagram. Teaser publication precision is September only, so reference publishedDate is null; the saved event dates the actual September 16 adviser announcement.

Anatole: correct request 24INR0355, Anatole Renewable Energy LLC, 207.82 MW bus / 200 MW POI. The original 25INR0398 belongs to inactive Large Pumpville Ranch 1 Solar, Val Verde. Downloaded December 10, 2024 PUCT SGIA filing identifies Eustace Southeast 138 kV, Rayburn and a POI about 2.59 miles southeast of Eustace on CR 2806. Native 200 MW follows explicit POI/operator scope; June 30, 2027 queue target differs from older operator 2026 / construction-planned-2025 statements. Saved the confirmed filing milestone, not a claim of construction or COD. Removed $210M, 831 MWh, four-hour and inferred Oncor. Operator site describes up to 20 acres but only publishes a stock Adobe image, rejected. Esri road-name geocode improves wrong county point but is explicitly road context, not exact battery parcel or the precise filing bearing.

NEO-04 16876 held: synthetic building-4 permit URL returns 404. The actual Ohio EPA P0137086 source, read in round 25, names Aligned NE001 Sandusky / 0322022037 and authorizes 186 backup generators across its scope. Operator supports a planned four-building campus, already represented by NEO-01 16724 and broader expansion 15776. No independently sourced fourth-building 110.4 MW / 96 MW IT, $3.65B or June 2030 COD. Retained counterparts unchanged. Their older tracker expansion ratings remain a dedicated follow-up, not validated by the hold.

PHX-03 16881 held: its synthetic permit URL returns 404, while current operator groups PHX-01/02/03 at 2500 W Union Hills Drive on 55 acres. This verifies the campus, not an independently rated 47.3 MW / 40 MW IT third-building pin with $1.28B and June 2024 COD. No automatic merge with Behrend, Waddell or Chandler. A dedicated building specification/permit or dated phase milestone is needed to restore this standalone tracker split. The hold does not imply campus cancellation.

PHX-07: exact operator address is 8785 N Reems Road, Waddell, not Union Hills. Opened general contractor Lewis project page describes phase PHX 07-2 as 40 MW IT / six halls / 214,078 sqft within an 80 MW two-phase project. Native 80 MW is that project scope, not all West Valley facilities, measured total demand or an additional 80 MW above phase two. Phase-two floor area is not assigned to the whole PHX07 record. Current operator gallery groups PHX01/02/03 elsewhere and is not borrowed. Two actual contractor construction aerials are used without inferring photo date, energization, generator count or completed fit-out.

Saved the dated report/publication milestone, not actual COD; removed December 2027 and $3.04B. The $86.5M land price is not construction cost. Direct requests return 403 while web-open retrieval succeeds. Census street interpolation differs from directory points and is explicitly address context, not surveyed building centroid. No unsupported APS 69 kV Union Hills substation attribution retained.

Caprock LBB01: opened April 9, 2026 operator groundbreaking release explicitly names first facility LBB01 / Q1 2027 target on 540 MW, 313-acre, six-facility, 1.65-million-sqft campus near Abernathy. Current official page, found through operator navigation at abernathy-tx-data-center, gives 1498 County Road 315, Abernathy. Corrected Plainview location and old December 2028 COD. No building-specific 108 MW / 96 MW IT rating, $3.42B or Xcel/SPP connection basis opened; native power deleted. Campus 540 MW is not divided by six. The expected $5B regional economic infusion is not LBB01 capital cost. Campus acreage remains explicitly shared. One campus-groundbreaking photo added; it does not show an operating LBB01.

Allium: current operator publishes 110 MW solar plus 110 MW battery on approximately 945 acres north of Hollister airport. Active CAISO request is 1921, with 112.491 MW solar / 112.386 MW battery / 110 MW combined export and Crazy Horse Canyon–Hollister 115 kV, not old 1532 / Panoche 230 kV. Prior Allium 1711 is withdrawn but does not cancel active 1921. Native 110 MW is solar only; no inferred installed 440 MWh. Operator timeline image targets end-2027 construction and near-end-2029 operation, versus active queue December 15, 2030; both explicit, no silently guaranteed schedule. Saved queue target as estimated and removed $150M / December 2027. No exact-name CA EIA plant match; similarly named Minnesota/Illinois entries rejected.
